page.text:
In formal axiomatic set theory, a set is taken as an undefined primitive.
We do not define what a set 'is' in terms of simpler components; instead,
its nature is entirely characterized by the membership relation: for any
objects $x$ and $X$, either $x \in X$ or $x \notin X$. Under the
principle of *pure* set theory adopted here, there are no 'atoms' or
'urelements' (entities with no members that are not themselves sets);
every element of a set is itself a set. The declaration below formalizes
the core structural commitments that define a set.
